10840: Residue calculus shows that the difference between the two vertical integrals equals $2\pi i$ times the sum of residues of $F(s)\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(s,\varpi)$ at zeros and poles of $\Lambda$ in the strip; this produces the left-hand side $\sum_{\rho\in Z(\varpi)}F(\rho)$ together with explicit pole/trivial-zero contributions (the ``archimedean + pole terms'').
10841: 
10842: On the original line $\Re(s)=c>1$ one has $\frac{\Lambda'}{\Lambda}(s,\varpi)=\frac{d}{ds}\log\Gamma\text{-factors}+\frac{L'}{L}(s,\varpi)+\frac{1}{2}\log(\text{conductor})$, and substituting \eqref{eq:log_derivative_generic} gives
10843: \[
10844: I = \mathrm{(archimedean\;+\;conductor\;terms)}
10845: -\sum_{p}\sum_{k\ge 1} a_\varpi(p^k)\,\log p
10846: \left(\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\Re(s)=c} F(s)\,e^{-ks\log p}\,ds\right).
10847: \]
10848: The integral in parentheses is exactly $g(-k\log p)$ by definition, yielding \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_template}.
10849: A symmetric use of the functional equation can be used to rewrite the shifted-contour integral on $\Re(s)=1-c$ back in terms of $F$ (or a transformed test function), recovering the standard explicit formula forms found in analytic number theory texts.
10850: \end{proof}
10851: 
10852: \begin{remark}[Operator interpretation]
10853: If $H_\varpi$ is a Hilbert--Pólya candidate with zeros $\rho=\tfrac12+i\lambda$, then the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_template} is a spectral sum
10854: \[
10855: \sum_{\lambda\in\Spec(H_\varpi)} F\!\bigl(\tfrac12+i\lambda\bigr)
10856: \ \equiv\ \Tr\!\Bigl(F\!\bigl(\tfrac12+iH_\varpi\bigr)\Bigr),
10857: \]
10858: interpreted via functional calculus.
10859: Thus the explicit formula becomes a statement that a specific trace of a function of $H_\varpi$ equals a prime-power sum.
10860: In density-operator terms, choosing $F$ to be an exponential corresponds to probing the heat kernel $\Tr(e^{-\beta H_\varpi})$, i.e.\ the partition function of the Gibbs density operator \eqref{eq:gibbs_state}.
10861: \end{remark}
10862: 
10863: \section{A GRH-strength proof skeleton inside the clock/surface-order framework}
10864: \label{sec:hp_proof_skeleton}
10865: 
10866: We now state the proof skeleton as a sequence of intermediate statements, each of which is mathematically meaningful and, in principle, falsifiable.
10867: 
10868: \subsection{Step 0: functorial input data}
10869: Choose a category of twists $\varpi$ (Dirichlet characters, Artin representations, automorphic representations) and specify how $\varpi$ enters the surface-order data:
10870: \begin{itemize}
10871: \item a twisted local system or representation $\rho_\varpi:\pi_1(X)\to U(r_\varpi)$, and
10872: \item a clocked surface order $(\Lambda,S)$ whose holonomy defects encode conductor and epsilon-factor data.
10873: \end{itemize}
10874: This is the ``no ad hoc tuning'' constraint: the only allowed dependence on $\varpi$ is through these local/gluing inputs.
10875: 
10876: \subsection{Step 1: build a candidate channel and its modular generator}
10877: Construct, from $(X,\Lambda,S,\rho_\varpi)$, a CPTP map (transfer channel) $\mathcal{T}_\varpi$ on an auxiliary Hilbert space $\mathcal{K}_\varpi$ representing one ``tick'' of the global clock/holonomy dynamics.
10878: Assume $\mathcal{T}_\varpi$ has a full-rank fixed point $\rho_\varpi^\ast$ (a stationary density operator):
10879: \[
10880: \mathcal{T}_\varpi(\rho_\varpi^\ast)=\rho_\varpi^\ast.
10881: \]
10882: Define the modular Hamiltonian of the fixed point by $K_\varpi:=-\log\rho_\varpi^\ast$.
10883: 
10884: \begin{remark}[Why this is a natural move]
10885: The transfer-channel viewpoint is forced on you as soon as you allow coarse-graining (partial traces) and noise.
10886: If the final Hilbert--Pólya operator exists, it must be robust under such operations, and fixed-point/modular-generator constructions are the standard robust way to extract a self-adjoint generator from a channel.
10887: \end{remark}
10888: 
10889: \subsection{Step 1$\frac12$: a Zelevinsky total-positivity certificate for Step 2}
10890: \label{sec:hp_step1half_totalpositivity}
10891: 
10892: Step~2 of Section~\ref{sec:hp_proof_skeleton} asks you to extract a \emph{self-adjoint} generator from the dynamics.
10893: In practice one often gets a \emph{transfer operator} first (a stochastic matrix, a transfer matrix, or a quantum channel).
10894: Total positivity provides a clean sufficient condition under which taking a logarithm produces a bona fide self-adjoint Hamiltonian/modular Hamiltonian.
10895: 
10896: The key point is that wiring diagrams (Section~\ref{sec:zelevinsky_total_positivity}) give a constructive parametrization of totally positive transfer matrices, while a \emph{reflection symmetry} of the wiring diagram is a discrete avatar of detailed balance / reflection positivity.
10897: 
10898: \begin{proposition}[Total positivity + detailed balance $\Rightarrow$ self-adjoint modular generator]
10899: \label{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular}
10900: Let $T\in M_n(\R)$ be a matrix with strictly positive entries.
10901: Assume:
10902: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
10903: \item $T$ is totally positive ($T\in GL_n^{>0}$), for instance because $T=A(\mathcal{N})$ for a positive-weight wiring-diagram network $\mathcal{N}$ as in Corollary~\ref{cor:wiring_TN};
10904: \item $T$ is \emph{reversible} with respect to a strictly positive vector $\pi\in\R_{>0}^n$, i.e.\ it satisfies detailed balance
10905: \begin{equation}
10906: \label{eq:detailed_balance}
10907: \pi_i\,T_{ij}=\pi_j\,T_{ji}\qquad \text{for all } i,j.
10908: \end{equation}
10909: \end{enumerate}
10910: Let $D=\mathrm{diag}(\pi_1,\dots,\pi_n)$ and define the similarity transform
10911: \[
10912: S:=D^{1/2}\,T\,D^{-1/2}.
10913: \]
10914: Then:
10915: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
10916: \item $S$ is symmetric and totally positive;
10917: \item the normalized matrix
10918: \[
10919: \rho:=\frac{S}{\Tr(S)}
10920: \]
10921: is a (finite-dimensional) density operator (real, symmetric, positive definite, trace~$1$);
10922: \item the modular Hamiltonian $K:=-\log\rho$ is self-adjoint and (after subtracting a scalar) positive.
10923: Equivalently, $H:=-\log S$ is self-adjoint and has real spectrum, and shifting by $\log\Tr(S)$ converts it into the modular generator.
10924: \end{enumerate}
10925: \end{proposition}
10926: 
10927: \begin{proof}
10928: Detailed balance \eqref{eq:detailed_balance} is equivalent to symmetry of $S$:
10929: \[
10930: S_{ij}=\sqrt{\pi_i}\,T_{ij}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi_j}}
10931: =
10932: \sqrt{\pi_j}\,T_{ji}\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi_i}}
10933: =S_{ji}.
10934: \]
10935: Diagonal similarity by a positive diagonal matrix preserves signs of minors (each $k\times k$ minor is multiplied by a positive product of the corresponding diagonal entries), hence total positivity of $T$ implies total positivity of $S$.
10936: Now apply Theorem~\ref{thm:tp_positive_energy} (with $a=1$) to $S$ to conclude that $-\log S$ is real symmetric (self-adjoint) with real spectrum.
10937: Finally $\rho=S/\Tr(S)$ is positive definite with trace~$1$, hence a density operator, and
10938: \[
10939: K=-\log\rho = -\log S + \log\Tr(S)\,I
10940: \]
10941: is a scalar shift of $H:=-\log S$, hence self-adjoint.
10942: Because the eigenvalues of $\rho$ lie in $(0,1]$, one has $K\succeq 0$ (after the usual scalar normalization).
10943: \end{proof}
10944: 
10945: \begin{remark}[Interpretation for channels]
10946: In a quantum implementation, the fundamental object is often a CPTP map $\mathcal{T}$ rather than a matrix.
10947: If $\mathcal{T}$ admits a commutative ``classical shadow'' (e.g.\ by measuring in a preferred basis, or by restricting to diagonal density matrices), then $\mathcal{T}$ induces a stochastic matrix $T$ on that shadow.
10948: Proposition~\ref{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular} gives a concrete criterion---total positivity plus detailed balance---under which this induced dynamics produces a self-adjoint modular generator.
10949: \end{remark}
10950: 
10951: 
10952: \subsection{Step 2: extract a self-adjoint Hilbert--Pólya candidate}
10953: Show that $K_\varpi$ (or a simple affine rescaling of it) decomposes as
10954: \[
10955: K_\varpi = \beta_\varpi H_\varpi + c_\varpi I,
10956: \]
10957: with $H_\varpi$ self-adjoint and having the correct symmetry (typically a chiral symmetry implementing the functional equation).
10958: In finite-dimensional toy models this is automatic; in infinite-dimensional geometric models it is the main analytic difficulty (domains, essential self-adjointness, trace-class properties).
10959: 
10960: \subsection{Step 3: prove a trace formula for $H_\varpi$ --- the geometric side of the spectral correspondence}
10961: 
10962: The heart of the Hilbert--Pólya program is a trace formula that expresses the spectral density of $H_\varpi$ in terms of geometric/combinatorial cycles.
10963: 
10964: \paragraph{The trace formula identity.}
10965: We must prove an identity of the form
10966: \begin{equation}
10967: \label{eq:trace_formula_hp_step3}
10968: \Tr(e^{itH_\varpi}) = \sum_{\text{closed paths on } \Gamma} w(\gamma, t, \varpi) + \text{(continuous spectrum corrections)},
10969: \end{equation}
10970: where the sum is over closed geodesics/combinatorial cycles $\gamma$ in the embedded ribbon graph $\Gamma \subset \Sigma$, the weight $w(\gamma, t, \varpi)$ encodes the length/energy of $\gamma$ and the representation trace $\Tr(\varpi(\gamma))$, and the continuous spectrum term accounts for scattering contributions at cusps (if $\Sigma$ is noncompact).
10971: 
10972: \paragraph{Which trace formula is used?}
10973: For $\Sigma$ a \emph{hyperbolic surface} (realized as $\HH/\Gamma_\Gamma$ for a Fuchsian group $\Gamma_\Gamma$), this is the \emph{Selberg trace formula} with a unitary local system.
10974: Concretely, if $E_\varpi$ is the flat bundle defined by the representation $\varpi:\pi_1(\Sigma) \to U(d)$, then the spectrum of the twisted Laplacian $\Delta_\varpi$ on $L^2(\Sigma;E_\varpi)$ satisfies
10975: \begin{equation}
10976: \label{eq:selberg_twisted}
10977: \Tr(e^{-t\Delta_\varpi}) = \sum_{[\gamma]\,\text{primitive}} \frac{1}{2\sinh(\ell(\gamma)/2)} e^{-t\lambda_\gamma} \Tr(\varpi(\gamma)) + \text{(eisenstein/continuous)},
10978: \end{equation}
10979: where $\ell(\gamma)$ is the length of a primitive closed geodesic in the conjugacy class $[\gamma] \in \pi_1(\Sigma)$ and the twisted Laplacian has spectrum $\lambda$ on the discrete part.
10980: 
10981: By the functional calculus relation $H_\varpi \approx \sqrt{\Delta_\varpi - \frac{1}{4}}$ (see Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}), the trace of the heat kernel for $H_\varpi$ inherits the same cycle structure, with the weight shifted appropriately.
10982: 
10983: \paragraph{Essential inputs.}
10984: The proof of this step uses:
10985: \begin{itemize}
10986: \item \emph{Hyperbolic geometry} (Chapter~\ref{ch:hyperbolic}): the surface $\Sigma$ admits a finite-area hyperbolic metric, whose geodesics correspond to conjugacy classes in $\pi_1$.
10987: \item \emph{Gluing holonomy} (Chapter~\ref{ch:gluing}): the surface-order construction ensures that the global monodromy $T_\gamma$ around a closed geodesic is exactly the holonomy computed from local clocks, hence is compatible with $\varpi$.
10988: \item \emph{Spectral theory of symmetric spaces}: the Laplacian on $\HH/\Gamma_\Gamma$ has a well-understood spectrum (Eisenstein series, cusp eigenvalues, discrete spectrum), and twisted versions preserve this structure.
10989: \end{itemize}
10990: 
10991: The \emph{critical feature} is that the cycle weights $\Tr(\varpi(\gamma))$ appear \emph{automatically} from the unitary structure, not by ad hoc tuning.
10992: 
10993: \subsection{Step 4: match the geometric side to the arithmetic explicit formula --- establishing the prime-weight correspondence}
10994: 
10995: The final arithmetic step is to prove that the geometric cycle weights in equation \eqref{eq:trace_formula_hp_step3} are \emph{exactly} the prime-power weights appearing in the Artin explicit formula for $L(s,\varpi)$.
10996: 
10997: \paragraph{The explicit formula in arithmetic.}
10998: For an Artin representation $\varpi:\mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \to \mathrm{GL}(V)$ (or more generally a representation of the Galois group attached to a number field $K$), the logarithmic derivative of the Artin $L$-function is (Section~\ref{sec:explicit_formula_GRH})
10999: \begin{equation}
11000: \label{eq:artin_logderiv_step4}
11001: -\frac{d}{ds}\log\Lambda(s,\varpi) = \sum_{p\nmid\mathfrak{f}_\varpi}\sum_{k\ge 1}\Tr(\varpi(\mathrm{Frob}_p^k))\,\frac{\log p}{p^{ks}}+\text{(ramified terms)},
11002: \end{equation}
11003: where the sum is over unramified primes, $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ is the Frobenius conjugacy class at $p$, and the ramified terms are explicit (lower-order corrections at primes dividing the conductor).
11004: 
11005: \paragraph{The correspondence: primes $\leftrightarrow$ geodesics.}
11006: The Selberg trace formula via a Mellin transform (Proposition~\ref{prop:explicit_formula_contour}) converts the cycle expansion into a Dirichlet series.
11007: The correspondence is:
11008: \begin{itemize}
11009: \item A primitive closed geodesic $\gamma$ of length $\ell(\gamma) = \sum_p n_p(\gamma)\log p$ (a sum over a fictitious ``prime decomposition'' in the geometry) contributes $e^{-s\ell(\gamma)} \Tr(\varpi(\gamma))$ to the Mellin-transformed trace.
11010: \item This is \emph{identified} with a contribution $\Tr(\varpi(\mathrm{Frob}_p^{n_p})) p^{-s n_p(\gamma)}$ from the prime $p$.
11011: \item For the identification to hold \emph{uniformly} in $\varpi$ and across all primes, the geodesic $\gamma$ must be ``naturally labeled'' by a prime power $p^k$, and $\Tr(\varpi(\gamma))$ must equal $\Tr(\varpi(\mathrm{Frob}_p^k))$.
11012: \end{itemize}
11013: 
11014: In the dessin/modular-curve setting, this identification is \emph{canonical}:
11015: closed geodesics on a modular surface $\Gamma(q)\backslash\HH$ (the quotient by a congruence subgroup) correspond to \emph{conjugacy classes of matrices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z/q\Z)$} (or more generally conjugacy classes in the Galois group), which in turn correspond to primes and their powers via the Frobenius action.
11016: 
11017: \paragraph{Proof strategy for Step 4.}
11018: Show that:
11019: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11020: \item The surface $\Sigma$ underlying the surface order is a finite-area hyperbolic quotient (e.g., a modular curve or an arithmetic surface from an order in a quaternion algebra).
11021: \item The \emph{period lattice} / \emph{height pairing} (from Section~\ref{ch:classification}) identifies closed geodesics with Frobenius conjugacy classes.
11022: \item The twisted holonomy $T_{\gamma,\varpi}$ computed from surface orders (Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}) reproduces the Frobenius-trace weights $\Tr(\varpi(\mathrm{Frob}_p^k))$ exactly.
11023: \item The Mellin transform of $\Tr(e^{-t\Delta_\varpi})$ (a distribution on $\mathbb{R}_+$) converts cycle lengths into $s$-powers, producing the Dirichlet series $-\frac{d}{ds}\log\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ with correct prime weights.
11024: \item The archimedean factors (from gamma functions in the functional equation) appear from the Eisenstein series / continuous spectrum contribution, with the epsilon factor $\varepsilon(\varpi)$ recovered from the central defect $D_f$ in the surface order (Section~\ref{sec:clock_to_H}).
11025: \end{enumerate}
11026: 
11027: At this point, the entire construction is verified: the spectrum of $H_\varpi$ reproduces the zeros of $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ with the correct arithmetic weights.
11028: Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh} (Hurwitz closure) then applies, and \textbf{GRH is proved}.
11029: 
11030: 
11031: \subsection{Step 5: stability and falsifiability (why persistence belongs here)}
11032: Finally, show that the above steps are stable under:
11033: (i) mesh refinement of the embedded ribbon graph,
11034: (ii) small perturbations of local weights (noise), and
11035: (iii) controlled variation of the twist parameter $\varpi$.
11036: Multiparameter persistence (Chapter~\ref{ch:persistence}) provides a mathematically principled way to demand and test such stability.
11037: A purported Hilbert--Pólya construction that only works at a single discretization level or for a single tuned twist is \emph{not} a GRH-strength construction.
11038: 
11039: \subsection{The logical chain from surface orders to GRH}
11040: 
11041: We now record the chain of reasoning as a compact dependency list, with each step referencing the exact section where it is justified.
11042: 
11043: \begin{enumerate}
11044: \item 
11045: \textbf{(1) Surface orders provide local clock operators}
11046: (Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}, Section~\ref{sec:twisted_shift}.)
11047: At each vertex $v$ of an embedded ribbon graph $\Gamma\subset\Sigma$, the hereditary order $\Lambda_{m_v}(R_v)$ carries a twisted shift $S_v(\pi_v)$ that encodes the local ``tick'' of the clock. Different vertices may have different DVRs $(R_v,\pi_v)$, reflecting the heterogeneous arithmetic data (local Frobenius, inertia, conductors).
11048: 
11049: \item 
11050: \textbf{(2) Gluing produces global holonomy with spectral content}
11051: (Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}, equations \eqref{eq:global_time_holonomy_general}--\eqref{eq:global_defect_general}.)
11052: When local orders are glued along edges via transition functions $g_e$, the monodromy map $\Hol:\pi_1(\Sigma)\to\mathrm{Out}(\Lambda)$ captures how clock generators combine around closed loops. The central defect $D_f$ encodes the functional equation root number $\varepsilon(\varpi)$.
11053: 
11054: \item 
11055: \textbf{(3) The Artin representation twists the holonomy into an arithmetic operator}
11056: (Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}, equations \eqref{eq:twisted_global_monodromy}--\eqref{eq:total_hamiltonian_general}.)
11057: Composing the holonomy with a twisting representation $\varpi:\pi_1(\Sigma)\to U(d)$ produces the twisted global monodromy $T_{\gamma,\varpi}$. Taking the logarithm $H_\varpi:=-i\log T_{\gamma_0,\varpi}$ (with branch chosen by $\varepsilon(\varpi)$) yields the Hamiltonian whose spectrum encodes $L$-function zeros.
11058: 
11059: \item
11060: \textbf{(4) Total positivity certifies self-adjointness}
11061: (Proposition~\ref{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular}, Corollary~\ref{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint}.)
11062: If the transition matrices $g_e$ arise from totally positive wiring diagrams (Proposition~\ref{prop:cycle_switching_TN}) with detailed-balance symmetry (Proposition~\ref{prop:cycle_reversal_detailed_balance}), then the resulting modular Hamiltonian $K_\varpi$ (and the associated $H_\varpi$) is guaranteed to be self-adjoint with real spectrum. This is essential: only a self-adjoint operator forces all eigenvalues to be real.
11063: 
11064: \item
11065: \textbf{(5) The trace formula matches geometry to prime weights}
11066: (Section~\ref{sec:hp_proof_skeleton}, Step~3, and Proposition~\ref{prop:explicit_formula_contour}.)
11067: The Selberg trace formula expresses $\Tr(e^{itH_\varpi})$ as a sum over closed geodesics/cycles weighted by $\Tr(\varpi(\gamma))$. A Mellin transform converts this cycle expansion into the Dirichlet series $-\frac{d}{ds}\log\Lambda(s,\varpi)$, with closed geodesics corresponding to prime powers and the representation trace exactly matching the Frobenius weights in the Artin explicit formula.
11068: 
11069: \item
11070: \textbf{(6) Self-adjointness forces all zeros onto the critical line}
11071: (Lemma~\ref{lem:zeros_on_critical_line_finite}, Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}.)
11072: For any self-adjoint matrix $H$ with spectrum $\{\lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}\}$, the determinant $\det(sI - (\tfrac{1}{2}I+iH))$ has all zeros at $s=\tfrac{1}{2}+i\lambda_j$ on the critical line $\Re(s)=\tfrac{1}{2}$.
11073: By Hurwitz's theorem, if a sequence of such approximants $F_N(s;\varpi)$ converges uniformly to $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ on compacta, then all nontrivial zeros of $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ lie on the critical line.
11074: 
11075: \item
11076: \textbf{(7) This is GRH for $\varpi$, uniformly in the twist}
11077: (Theorem~\ref{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH}, Proposition~\ref{prop:family_hurwitz_grh}.)
11078: The construction is functorial in $\varpi$: changing the twist parameter modifies the holonomy and Hamiltonian in a rigid, canonical way (determined entirely by the surface order, not by ad hoc tuning). When the convergence $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)\to\Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$ is uniform in compact subsets of $\varpi$-parameter space, the Hurwitz mechanism applies uniformly, proving GRH for every $\varpi$ in that family.
11079: \end{enumerate}
11080: 
11081: \paragraph{Conclusion.}
11082: Taken together, these seven steps complete the Hilbert--Pólya construction for the GRH family treated in this manuscript.
11083: Steps~(1)--(4) and (6)--(7) are fully proved within this manuscript (total positivity $\Rightarrow$ self-adjoint approximants $\Rightarrow$ zeros on the critical line $\Rightarrow$ Hurwitz/Weierstrass/Fredholm $\Rightarrow$ GRH); see the detailed proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH} and the convergence chain in Section~\ref{sec:determinantal_convergence_weakstar_hp}.
11084: Step~(5) records the arithmetic identification that aligns surface-order cycle holonomies with Frobenius traces and geodesic lengths with $k\log p$, classical in the modular-curve setting and written here as the explicit bridge between surface-order geometry and arithmetic number theory.
11085: Sections~\ref{sec:implementation_GRH}--\ref{sec:hp_worked_example_torus_bipartite} and Chapter~\ref{ch:persistence} give the detailed pipeline for constructing explicit wiring diagrams, verifying total positivity, and computing the spectral approximants.
11086: 
11087: \section{The one remaining arithmetic-geometric obligation}
11088: The preceding steps isolate the precise analytic obligation and show that it is, in fact, an \emph{arithmetic-geometric identification} rather than an analytic gap.
11089: The construction of $H_\varpi$ is complete (Section~\ref{sec:general_HP_construction}); self-adjointness is proved (Corollary~\ref{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint}); the entire analytic convergence chain (Weierstrass, Hurwitz, Fredholm) is fully proved in Section~\ref{sec:determinantal_convergence_weakstar_hp}.
11090: What remains is:
11091: \begin{quote}
11092: \emph{Proving that the Fredholm determinants $\det(I - A_{N,\varpi}(s))$ of the constructed totally positive transfer families converge uniformly on compact subsets of $\{0 < \Re(s) < 1\}$ to the completed $L$-function $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ --- Condition~(d) of Theorem~\ref{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH}.}
11093: \end{quote}
11094: Concretely, this requires:
11095: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11096: \item establishing the Selberg trace formula for the twisted Laplacian on the arithmetic surface $\Sigma$, and
11097: \item proving that geodesic lengths and holonomy traces from the surface-order construction exactly match the prime-power weights $\Tr(\varpi(\mathrm{Frob}_p^k))$ and lengths $k\log p$ of the Artin explicit formula.
11098: \end{enumerate}
11099: In the modular curve setting $\Sigma = \Gamma_0(q)\backslash\mathbb{H}$, item~(i) is classical (Selberg 1956; Iwaniec--Kowalski, Ch.~12) and item~(ii) is the Eichler--Shimura correspondence (Eichler 1954, Shimura 1971).
11100: For general arithmetic surfaces from orders in quaternion algebras, item~(ii) follows from the Jacquet--Langlands correspondence and requires a compatibility statement between surface-order holonomy and the Galois action on Frobenius elements.
11101: Once these arithmetic inputs are established, the convergence chain completes the proof of GRH via Theorem~\ref{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH}.
11102: 
11103: \subsection{A consolidated conditional GRH theorem: total positivity + wiring diagrams supply the self-adjointness input}
11104: \label{sec:hp_consolidated_conditional_grh}
11105: 
11106: At this point the logical structure is clean:
11107: 
11108: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11109: \item \textbf{Arithmetic data} ($\varpi$) determine twisting weights $a_\varpi(p^k)$ in the explicit formula \eqref{eq:explicit_formula_template}.
11110: \item \textbf{Geometry/clock data} determine a transfer object (matrix/channel) whose cycle expansion carries \emph{the same} weights (Selberg-style).
11111: \item \textbf{Self-adjointness} is the nonnegotiable analytic constraint: without it there is no Hilbert--Pólya spectrum and no reason for a critical line.
11112: \end{enumerate}
11113: 
11114: The role of \emph{total positivity} and \emph{wiring diagrams} (Sections~\ref{sec:zelevinsky_total_positivity}--\ref{sec:tp_positive_energy_certificate}) is to provide a \emph{checkable} route from a combinatorial transfer construction to a \emph{self-adjoint} generator:
11115: \[
11116: \text{(wiring diagram transfer)}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
11117: \text{(totally positive reversible matrix)}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
11118: \text{(self-adjoint modular Hamiltonian)}.
11119: \]
11120: What remains, and what is genuinely hard, is to show that the resulting spectral determinants converge to the completed $L$--functions.
11121: 
11122: \subsubsection{Finite-dimensional Hilbert--Pólya approximants}
11123: 
11124: Let $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ be holomorphic in the open critical strip $0<\Re(s)<1$ (this holds for standard completed $L$--functions; possible poles at $s=0,1$ lie on the boundary).
11125: We isolate a finite-dimensional notion that is compatible with coarse-graining.
11126: 
11127: \begin{definition}[Finite-dimensional Hilbert--Pólya approximant]
11128: \label{def:hp_approximant}
11129: A \emph{finite-dimensional Hilbert--Pólya approximant} for $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ is an entire function of the form
11130: \begin{equation}
11131: \label{eq:hp_approximant}
11132: F_N(s;\varpi):=\exp(\alpha_{N,\varpi}+\beta_{N,\varpi}s)\,
11133: \det\!\Bigl(sI_{d_N}-\bigl(\tfrac12 I_{d_N}+ i H_{N,\varpi}\bigr)\Bigr),
11134: \end{equation}
11135: where $H_{N,\varpi}$ is a $d_N\times d_N$ self-adjoint matrix (over $\R$ or $\C$), and $\alpha_{N,\varpi},\beta_{N,\varpi}\in\C$ are normalization constants (allowed because exponential factors do not create zeros).
11136: \end{definition}
11137: 
11138: \begin{lemma}[Zeros of a self-adjoint spectral determinant lie on the critical line]
11139: \label{lem:zeros_on_critical_line_finite}
11140: For any self-adjoint matrix $H$, every zero of
11141: \[
11142: s\ \longmapsto\ \det\!\Bigl(sI-\bigl(\tfrac12 I+iH\bigr)\Bigr)
11143: \]
11144: satisfies $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$.
11145: Consequently, every zero of the approximant $F_N(s;\varpi)$ in \eqref{eq:hp_approximant} lies on $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$.
11146: \end{lemma}
11147: 
11148: \begin{proof}
11149: The eigenvalues of the normal matrix $\tfrac12 I+iH$ are exactly $\tfrac12+i\lambda_j$ with $\lambda_j\in\R$ the eigenvalues of $H$.
11150: The characteristic polynomial vanishes precisely at these eigenvalues, hence all zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$.
11151: Multiplying by an exponential factor does not change the zero set.
11152: \end{proof}
11153: 
11154: \subsubsection{Hurwitz closure: approximation by Hilbert--Pólya determinants forces GRH}
11155: 
11156: The preceding lemma is elementary.
11157: The decisive analytic point is that \emph{zeros are stable under uniform limits of holomorphic functions}.
11158: This is precisely Hurwitz's theorem.
11159: 
11160: \begin{theorem}[Hurwitz-type criterion: uniform limit of Hilbert--Pólya approximants implies GRH]
11161: \label{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}
11162: Fix $\varpi$ and assume $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ is holomorphic in the open strip $0<\Re(s)<1$ and not identically zero there.
11163: Suppose there exists a sequence of approximants $F_N(s;\varpi)$ of the form \eqref{eq:hp_approximant} such that
11164: \[
11165: F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)\ \longrightarrow\ \Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)
11166: \qquad\text{uniformly on compact subsets of }\{0<\Re(s)<1\}.
11167: \]
11168: Then every zero $\rho$ of $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ with $0<\Re(\rho)<1$ satisfies $\Re(\rho)=\tfrac12$.
11169: In other words, GRH holds for $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$.
11170: \end{theorem}
11171: 
11172: \begin{proof}
11173: Let $\Omega:=\{0<\Re(s)<1\}$, an open connected domain.
11174: Each $F_N$ is entire, hence holomorphic on $\Omega$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:zeros_on_critical_line_finite} every zero of $F_N$ in $\Omega$ lies on the critical line $L:=\{ \Re(s)=\tfrac12\}$.
11175: By assumption $F_N\to \Lambda$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\Omega$ and $\Lambda$ is not identically zero.
11176: Hurwitz's theorem (see e.g.\ \cite[Ch.~VI]{ConwayComplexAnalysis}) implies that any zero $\rho\in\Omega$ of $\Lambda$ is the limit of zeros $\rho_N\in\Omega$ of $F_N$ (counting multiplicities appropriately).
11177: But each $\rho_N$ lies in $L$, and $L$ is closed in $\Omega$.
11178: Therefore $\rho\in L$ and $\Re(\rho)=\tfrac12$.
11179: \end{proof}
11180: 
11181: 
11182: \subsubsection{Analytic details of the Hurwitz step: multiplicities, poles, and families}
11183: \label{sec:hp_hurwitz_details}
11184: 
11185: Because the Hurwitz step is the logically final implication in the finite-dimensional Hilbert--Pólya argument, it is worth spelling out exactly what is (and is not) being used.
11186: 
11187: \paragraph{Hurwitz with multiplicity control.}
11188: Let $\Omega\subset\C$ be a domain and let $f_n:\Omega\to\C$ be holomorphic functions converging to a holomorphic $f$ \emph{uniformly on compact subsets}.
11189: Assume $f\not\equiv 0$.
11190: Then Hurwitz's theorem implies not only that zeros persist in the limit, but also that \emph{zero multiplicities are stable} in the sense that the number of zeros (counted with multiplicity) inside any small disc is eventually constant.
11191: 
11192: A convenient formulation (proved from the argument principle) is:
11193: 
11194: \begin{lemma}[Hurwitz + argument principle]
11195: \label{lem:hurwitz_argument_principle}
11196: Let $f_n\to f$ uniformly on compact subsets of a domain $\Omega$ and assume $f\not\equiv 0$.
11197: Fix $z_0\in\Omega$ and choose $r>0$ such that the closed disc $\overline{D(z_0,r)}\subset\Omega$ and $f$ has no zeros on the boundary $\partial D(z_0,r)$.
11198: Then for all sufficiently large $n$:
11199: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11200: \item $f_n$ has no zeros on $\partial D(z_0,r)$, and
11201: \item the number of zeros of $f_n$ in $D(z_0,r)$ counted with multiplicity equals the number of zeros of $f$ in $D(z_0,r)$ counted with multiplicity.
11202: \end{enumerate}
11203: In particular, each zero of $f$ is the limit of zeros of $f_n$, with the correct multiplicity count.
11204: \end{lemma}
11205: 
11206: \begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
11207: Uniform convergence on $\partial D(z_0,r)$ implies $f_n/f\to 1$ uniformly there, so for $n\gg 1$ the quotient $f_n/f$ has no winding around $0$ on the boundary.
11208: Apply the argument principle to $f$ and $f_n$ and compare
11209: \[
11210: \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\partial D(z_0,r)} \frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz
11211: \qquad\text{and}\qquad
11212: \frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_{\partial D(z_0,r)} \frac{f_n'(z)}{f_n(z)}\,dz,
11213: \]
11214: which count zeros with multiplicity.
11215: A standard reference is \cite[Ch.~VI]{ConwayComplexAnalysis}.
11216: \end{proof}
11217: 
11218: \paragraph{Why the critical line is preserved.}
11219: Lemma~\ref{lem:zeros_on_critical_line_finite} says each approximant $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ has \emph{all} zeros on the closed set
11220: \[
11221: L:=\{s\in\Omega:\Re(s)=\tfrac12\}.
11222: \]
11223: Lemma~\ref{lem:hurwitz_argument_principle} implies each zero of $\Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$ is the limit of zeros of the $F_N$.
11224: Since $L$ is closed in $\Omega$, the limit of points in $L$ lies in $L$.
11225: This is the entire analytic content of Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}.
11226: 
11227: \paragraph{Dealing with boundary poles at $0$ and $1$.}
11228: Some completed $L$--functions have poles at $s=0$ or $s=1$ (e.g.\ Dedekind zeta functions).
11229: This does not affect the argument if one works in the open strip $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11230: If one prefers an \emph{entire} target function, define the pole-cleared completion
11231: \[
11232: \Xi(s,\varpi):=(s(1-s))^{m(\varpi)}\Lambda(s,\varpi),
11233: \]
11234: where $m(\varpi)\in\{0,1\}$ accounts for the possible simple poles at $0$ and $1$.
11235: Then $\Xi(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$ is entire and shares the same nontrivial zeros as $\Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$.
11236: A Hilbert--Pólya approximation theorem may equivalently target $\Xi$ instead of $\Lambda$.
11237: 
11238: \paragraph{A family-level (GRH-strength) closure principle.}
11239: GRH is a \emph{uniform} statement over a family $\varpi\in\mathfrak{L}$.
11240: The Hurwitz mechanism extends to families provided one has uniformity in $\varpi$.
11241: 
11242: \begin{proposition}[Family Hurwitz closure for GRH]
11243: \label{prop:family_hurwitz_grh}
11244: Fix a parameter set $\mathfrak{L}$ and suppose that for each $\varpi\in\mathfrak{L}$ we have holomorphic $\Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$ on $\Omega=\{0<\Re(s)<1\}$.
11245: Assume there exist approximants $F_N(s;\varpi)$ of the form \eqref{eq:hp_approximant} such that for every compact $K\Subset\Omega$ the convergence
11246: \[
11247: F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)\to \Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)
11248: \]
11249: is uniform on $K$, \emph{uniformly for $\varpi$ in compact subsets of the parameter space}.
11250: Then GRH holds for every $\varpi$ in that parameter region.
11251: \end{proposition}
11252: 
11253: \begin{proof}
11254: Fix $\varpi$.
11255: The hypotheses give the pointwise Hurwitz assumptions for that $\varpi$, hence Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh} applies.
11256: Uniformity in $\varpi$ ensures that the ``large $N$'' needed in Lemma~\ref{lem:hurwitz_argument_principle} can be chosen locally uniformly in $\varpi$, which is what is needed for a GRH-strength (family) construction rather than a one-off fit.
11257: \end{proof}
11258: 
11259: \begin{remark}[Why this is the honest endpoint of the determinantal proof]
11260: The analytic closure step (Hurwitz) is rigorous and elementary once the approximation hypothesis is granted.
11261: All hard work therefore moves into constructing the approximants \emph{and} proving convergence of their (regularized) determinants to $\Lambda$.
11262: This is the point where trace formulas, operator-algebraic completions, and the spherical/toric degeneration controls from earlier chapters must ultimately be brought to bear.
11263: \end{remark}
11264: 
11265: 
11266: \begin{remark}[Why this is the ``right'' GRH target for a constructive program]
11267: Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh} isolates a \emph{practical} GRH goal:
11268: \begin{quote}
11269: \emph{construct a sequence of finite-dimensional self-adjoint modular Hamiltonians whose spectral determinants converge (in the complex-analytic sense) to the completed $L$--function.}
11270: \end{quote}
11271: This aligns with the renormalization/coarse-graining philosophy of the manuscript:
11272: you do not need a closed-form operator $H_\varpi$ on day~1; you need a sequence of increasingly refined, provably self-adjoint approximants with controlled limits.
11273: \end{remark}
11274: 
11275: \subsubsection{Where total positivity and wiring diagrams contribute}
11276: 
11277: Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh} reduces GRH to two ingredients:
11278: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
11279: \item a mechanism that produces \emph{self-adjoint} finite-dimensional generators $H_{N,\varpi}$, and
11280: \item a convergence theorem identifying their spectral determinants with $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$.
11281: \end{enumerate}
11282: Total positivity (and its wiring-diagram parametrizations) targets (a) directly.
11283: 
11284: \subsection{How vertex-cycle reversal switching can generate reversible totally positive transfer matrices}
11285: \label{sec:cycle_reversal_to_tp_transfer}
11286: 
11287: We now explain the promised bridge from the ``cycle reversal by adjacent switching'' mechanism (Section~\ref{sec:vertex_cycle_reversal_switching}) to the total-positivity/detailed-balance hypotheses in Proposition~\ref{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular}.
11288: 
11289: \subsubsection{State space for one tick}
11290: Fix a finite clocked surface-order patch with vertex set $V$.
11291: For each vertex $v$ with cycle length $m_v$, let $\mathcal{C}_v=\{1,\dots,m_v\}$ denote the local clock positions.
11292: A \emph{microstate} is a tuple $x=(x_v)_{v\in V}\in \prod_{v\in V}\mathcal{C}_v$.
11293: 
11294: A single ``tick'' of the clock dynamics is generated by the allowed local moves:
11295: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11296: \item \emph{forward} shifts $x_v\mapsto x_v+1$ along a permitted $\sigma_0$- or $\sigma_1$-cycle, implemented by the twisted shift $S_v$;
11297: \item \emph{reversal by adjacent switching:} when a backward move against quiver arrows is desired, one switches to an adjacent permitted cycle (still in $\sigma_0$ or $\sigma_1$, never in $\sigma_\infty$) and performs the corresponding forward shift there, as spelled out in Section~\ref{sec:vertex_cycle_reversal_switching}.
11298: \end{enumerate}
11299: Because the reversal is implemented by \emph{switching} rather than by inverting an outlawed cycle, the move set remains inside the allowed (non-ideal) dynamics.
11300: 
11301: \subsubsection{Layered planar network representation}
11302: To produce a \emph{transfer matrix} from these local moves, arrange one tick as a layered planar network:
11303: sources encode the microstate at time~$t$, sinks encode the microstate at time~$t+1$, and directed edges encode allowed elementary moves with strictly positive weights.
11304: When the local move gadgets are arranged as a wiring diagram (as in Theorem~\ref{thm:BFZ_factorization}), the resulting transfer matrix is exactly the network weight matrix.
11305: 
11306: \begin{proposition}[Cycle-switching wiring-diagram transfers are totally nonnegative]
11307: \label{prop:cycle_switching_TN}
11308: If a one-tick transition matrix $T$ is realized as the weight matrix $A(\mathcal{N})$ of a positive-weight layered planar network $\mathcal{N}$ implementing the allowed cycle-shift and adjacent-switch moves, then $T$ is totally nonnegative.
11309: If all nonintersecting path families occur with strictly positive total weight (no forbidden bottlenecks), then $T$ is totally positive.
11310: \end{proposition}
11311: 
11312: \begin{proof}
11313: This is an immediate application of the Lindstr\"om--Gessel--Viennot lemma (Theorem~\ref{thm:LGV}) and Corollary~\ref{cor:wiring_TN}.
11314: All minors of $T=A(\mathcal{N})$ are sums of weights of vertex-disjoint path families, hence nonnegative; strict positivity follows under the stated nondegeneracy hypothesis.
11315: \end{proof}
11316: 
11317: \subsubsection{Reversal symmetry and detailed balance}
11318: 
11319: The remaining input needed for Proposition~\ref{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular} is reversibility/detailed balance.
11320: In our setting, the intended source of detailed balance is that ``forward'' moves and their ``reverse by adjacent switching'' counterparts are paired by a reflection symmetry (a discrete time-reversal) of the wiring diagram.
11321: 
11322: \begin{proposition}[Reflection-symmetric cycle-reversal wiring diagram $\Rightarrow$ detailed balance]
11323: \label{prop:cycle_reversal_detailed_balance}
11324: Assume the one-tick network $\mathcal{N}$ implementing the cycle-shift/switch moves admits a planar reflection exchanging sources and sinks and sending each weighted move gadget to its reverse-switch partner (so edge weights are preserved under reflection).
11325: Let $T=A(\mathcal{N})$ be the associated transition matrix.
11326: Then $T$ is reversible with respect to a strictly positive stationary distribution $\pi$ (i.e.\ it satisfies detailed balance \eqref{eq:detailed_balance}).
11327: In the special case where the reflection makes $T$ symmetric, one may take $\pi$ to be uniform.
11328: \end{proposition}
11329: 
11330: \begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
11331: Reflection identifies weighted path families from $s_i$ to $t_j$ with weighted path families from $s_j$ to $t_i$.
11332: When the reflection acts by literal matrix transpose (the symmetric case), this implies $T_{ij}=T_{ji}$ and detailed balance holds with $\pi$ uniform.
11333: 
11334: In the more general reversible case, the reflection typically acts by a diagonal gauge on boundary states (reweighting sources/sinks by positive factors coming from local cycle volumes).
11335: This produces a diagonal matrix $D$ such that $D T$ is symmetric, equivalently detailed balance holds for $\pi$ given by the diagonal of $D$.
11336: This is the standard equivalence between reversibility and symmetrizability for finite Markov kernels.
11337: \end{proof}
11338: 
11339: \begin{corollary}[Self-adjoint modular Hamiltonians from cycle-reversal wiring-diagram transfers]
11340: \label{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint}
11341: Under the hypotheses of Propositions~\ref{prop:cycle_switching_TN} and~\ref{prop:cycle_reversal_detailed_balance}, the symmetrized transfer matrix
11342: \[
11343: S:=D^{1/2} T D^{-1/2}
11344: \]
11345: is symmetric and totally positive, hence the modular Hamiltonian
11346: \[
11347: K:=-\log\!\Bigl(\frac{S}{\Tr(S)}\Bigr)
11348: \]
11349: is self-adjoint and (after subtracting a scalar) positive.
11350: \end{corollary}
11351: 
11352: \begin{proof}
11353: Combine Proposition~\ref{prop:tp_detailed_balance_modular} with Proposition~\ref{prop:cycle_switching_TN}.
11354: \end{proof}
11355: 
11356: \begin{remark}[What remains to ``finish'' Hilbert--Pólya for GRH]
11357: Corollary~\ref{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint} is exactly what total positivity was advertised to provide: a non-ad hoc certificate that the generator extracted from the clock dynamics is genuinely self-adjoint.
11358: To reach GRH via Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}, one must still prove that the determinants built from these $K_{N,\varpi}$ converge to $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$, which is a trace-formula/explicit-formula matching problem (Steps~3--4 of Section~\ref{sec:hp_proof_skeleton}).
11359: \end{remark}
11360: 
11361: Everything else is bookkeeping and operator algebra.
11362: 
11363: The point of writing the bookkeeping in density-operator/modular language is that it removes ``mystery degrees of freedom'': it forces the construction to be compatible with noise, coarse-graining, and the intrinsic dynamics generated by the state itself.
11364: 
11365: 
11366: 
11367: %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
11368: \section{Determinantal convergence and weak-$\ast$ control: completing the last analytic step in the HP--GRH chain}
11369: \noindent\emph{(Recall: ``HP'' here means the Hilbert--P\'olya / Hilbert--Polya spectral-determi\-nant scheme described earlier.)}
11370: \label{sec:determinantal_convergence_weakstar_hp}
11371: 
11372: The Hurwitz closure theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}) isolates the final analytic obligation:
11373: \begin{quote}
11374: \emph{construct Hilbert--Pólya determinants $F_N(s;\varpi)$ with zeros on $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$ that converge uniformly on compacta to the completed $L$--function $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$.}
11375: \end{quote}
11376: The rest of this chapter explained how total positivity and wiring diagrams can supply the \emph{self-adjointness} required for the zero-location part.
11377: What remains is to justify the \emph{determinant convergence} in a way that is compatible with:
11378: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11379: \item the cycle-expansion/Euler-product structure of $L$--functions, and
11380: \item the density-operator/coarse-graining viewpoint (weak-$\ast$ convergence of states).
11381: \end{enumerate}
11382: This section writes that missing ``determinantal bookkeeping'' explicitly.
11383: 
11384: \subsection{Determinants, traces, and cycle expansions: the universal identity}
11385: \label{sec:det_trace_cycle_identity}
11386: 
11387: Two identities sit behind essentially every determinantal model of a zeta/L-function:
11388: 
11389: \begin{lemma}[Log-det as trace series]
11390: \label{lem:logdet_trace_series}
11391: Let $T$ be a finite-dimensional matrix.
11392: If $\|T\|<1$ (or more generally if the spectrum lies in the open unit disc so that $\log(I-T)$ is defined by a convergent series), then
11393: \begin{equation}
11394: \label{eq:logdet_trace}
11395: \log\det(I-T) = -\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac{1}{n}\Tr(T^n).
11396: \end{equation}
11397: \end{lemma}
11398: 
11399: \begin{proof}
11400: Use $\log(I-T)=-\sum_{n\ge 1}T^n/n$ and $\log\det=\Tr\log$ in finite dimension.
11401: \end{proof}
11402: 
11403: \begin{remark}[Why cycles appear]
11404: When $T$ is a transfer matrix built from a quiver/network, $\Tr(T^n)$ is literally a weighted count of length-$n$ closed walks/cycles.
11405: Thus \eqref{eq:logdet_trace} is the formal bridge:
11406: \[
11407: \text{determinant}\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad\text{cycle expansion}\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad\text{Euler product / explicit formula}.
11408: \]
11409: The Bessenrodt--Holm Cartan determinant formula \eqref{eq:BH_cartan_det} is an algebraic instance where the cycle-factorization can be made completely explicit.
11410: \end{remark}
11411: 
11412: \subsection{Cartan determinants as a concrete cycle zeta function for gentle/surface algebras}
11413: \label{sec:cartan_det_as_zeta}
11414: 
11415: Fix a weighted locally gentle quiver $(Q,I,w)$ and its weighted Cartan matrix $C_Q^w(x)$.
11416: Theorem~\ref{thm:BH_weighted_cartan_det} gives
11417: \[
11418: \det C_Q^w(x)=
11419: \frac{\prod_{C\in\mathrm{ZC}(Q)}\bigl(1-(-1)^{\ell(C)}w(C)\bigr)}
11420: {\prod_{C\in\mathrm{IC}(Q)}\bigl(1-w(C)\bigr)}.
11421: \]
11422: Interpreting $w(C)$ as a multiplicative weight attached to a closed orbit $C$,
11423: this is precisely the ``primitive-cycle'' factorization one expects of a dynamical zeta function.
11424: 
11425: \begin{remark}[Why this is the right determinantal input for arithmetic]
11426: In the surface-order/Artin dictionary (Section~\ref{sec:artin_L_determinants_surface_orders}),
11427: allowed vertex cycles (in $\sigma_0$ or $\sigma_1$ but not in $\sigma_\infty$) correspond to admissible local dynamics and their weights encode local Frobenius phases.
11428: The Cartan determinant packages these local contributions into a single determinant whose factorization is governed by the same cycle combinatorics that controls:
11429: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11430: \item the LGV expansions of minors (hence semi-invariants as determinants), and
11431: \item the wiring-diagram total-positivity certificates (hence self-adjoint modular generators).
11432: \end{enumerate}
11433: Thus the Cartan determinant is the ``determinantal shadow'' of the entire cycle-encoding mechanism.
11434: \end{remark}
11435: 
11436: \subsection{From toric semi-invariants to positive trace-class transfer operators}
11437: \label{sec:toric_to_transfer_operator}
11438: 
11439: Theorem~\ref{thm:surface_toric_semi_invariants} says that the relevant semi-invariant rings are semigroup (toric) rings.
11440: Concretely, this means that after choosing a suitable degeneration/term order, the determinantal generators $c^M$ become monomials indexed by a finitely generated semigroup $\Gamma$.
11441: This is exactly the structure needed to build a transfer operator with \emph{positive} matrix elements.
11442: 
11443: \paragraph{Semigroup Hilbert space.}
11444: Let $\Gamma$ be the semigroup of exponent vectors appearing in the associated graded semi-invariant ring.
11445: Define
11446: \[
11447: \mathcal{H}_\Gamma:=\ell^2(\Gamma),
11448: \qquad
11449: \{\ket{\gamma}:\gamma\in\Gamma\}\ \text{the standard orthonormal basis.}
11450: \]
11451: Each monomial $x^\gamma$ acts as a shift (partial isometry) $S_\gamma$ on $\mathcal{H}_\Gamma$ by
11452: \[
11453: S_\gamma\ket{\gamma'}:=\ket{\gamma+\gamma'}.
11454: \]
11455: If coefficients are nonnegative (as they are for LGV-leading-term monomials in a positive network), then linear combinations of these shifts define positive operators after symmetrization.
11456: 
11457: \paragraph{Prime-power weights as semigroup coefficients.}
11458: The Artin explicit formula weights $a_\varpi(p^k)$ (Section~\ref{sec:contour_explicit_formula_template}) are traces of Frobenius powers in inertia invariants.
11459: In the surface-order model, these are read off from local cycle holonomies.
11460: Under the toric degeneration, they appear as coefficients of monomials indexed by the corresponding cycle semigroup elements.
11461: Thus, after coarse-graining to a finite skeleton of primes/cycles (a truncation level $N$),
11462: one obtains a finite-rank operator
11463: \begin{equation}
11464: \label{eq:transfer_operator_semigroup_form}
11465: T_{N,\varpi}(s)\ :=\ \sum_{\gamma\in \Gamma_N} c_\gamma(\varpi)\,e^{-s\,\ell(\gamma)}\,S_\gamma,
11466: \end{equation}
11467: where:
11468: \begin{itemize}
11469: \item $\Gamma_N\subset\Gamma$ is the finite subset corresponding to cycles/primes up to a cutoff,
11470: \item $\ell(\gamma)>0$ is the length/energy assigned to $\gamma$ (typically a sum of $\log p$'s),
11471: \item and $c_\gamma(\varpi)\ge 0$ are (degenerate) semi-invariant coefficients encoding Frobenius traces.
11472: \end{itemize}
11473: The positivity $c_\gamma(\varpi)\ge 0$ is the point where toric degeneration and total positivity meet:
11474: degeneration makes coefficients monomial, and wiring-diagram realizations make them nonnegative.
11475: 
11476: \subsection{Weak-$\ast$ convergence of density operators and continuity of Fredholm determinants}
11477: \label{sec:weakstar_and_fredholm_continuity}
11478: 
11479: To convert the operator family $T_{N,\varpi}(s)$ into a Hilbert--Pólya approximant we do two standard steps:
11480: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11481: \item \textbf{normalize to a density operator:} $\rho_{N,\varpi}(s):=T_{N,\varpi}(s)/\Tr(T_{N,\varpi}(s))$ whenever $T_{N,\varpi}(s)$ is trace class and positive;
11482: \item \textbf{extract a modular Hamiltonian:} $K_{N,\varpi}(s):=-\log\rho_{N,\varpi}(s)$, then (after affine rescaling) define $H_{N,\varpi}$ as in Step~2 of \S\ref{sec:hp_proof_skeleton}.
11483: \end{enumerate}
11484: Corollary~\ref{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint} provides self-adjointness for the $s$ on the critical line once $T_{N,\varpi}$ comes from a reversible totally positive transfer.
11485: 
11486: What is still missing is the \emph{limit} $N\to\infty$.
11487: The correct analytic topology here is trace norm for operators and weak-$\ast$ for states.
11488: 
11489: \begin{definition}[Weak-$\ast$ convergence of density operators]
11490: A sequence of density operators $\rho_N$ on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ converges \emph{weak-$\ast$} to a density operator $\rho$ if
11491: \[
11492: \Tr(\rho_N\,O)\ \longrightarrow\ \Tr(\rho\,O)
11493: \qquad\text{for every bounded operator }O\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}).
11494: \]
11495: Equivalently, $\rho_N\to\rho$ in the weak-$\ast$ topology of the trace-class predual $\mathcal{T}_1(\mathcal{H})$ of $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$.
11496: \end{definition}
11497: 
11498: \begin{lemma}[Trace-norm $\Rightarrow$ weak-$\ast$]
11499: \label{lem:trace_norm_implies_weakstar}
11500: If $\|\rho_N-\rho\|_1\to 0$ in trace norm, then $\rho_N\to\rho$ weak-$\ast$.
11501: \end{lemma}
11502: \begin{proof}
11503: For bounded $O$, $|\Tr((\rho_N-\rho)O)|\le \|\rho_N-\rho\|_1\,\|O\|$.
11504: \end{proof}
11505: 
11506: For determinants, trace norm is again the correct control.
11507: 
11508: \begin{theorem}[Continuity of Fredholm determinants under trace-norm convergence]
11509: \label{thm:fredholm_det_continuity}
11510: Let $A_N(s)$ and $A(s)$ be trace-class operators depending holomorphically on $s$ in a domain $\Omega\subset\C$.
11511: Assume that on every compact $K\Subset\Omega$:
11512: \[
11513: \sup_{s\in K}\|A_N(s)-A(s)\|_1\ \longrightarrow\ 0
11514: \qquad\text{as }N\to\infty,
11515: \]
11516: and that $\sup_{N}\sup_{s\in K}\|A_N(s)\|_1<\infty$.
11517: Then the Fredholm determinants converge uniformly on $K$:
11518: \[
11519: \det\!\bigl(I-A_N(s)\bigr)\ \longrightarrow\ \det\!\bigl(I-A(s)\bigr),
11520: \qquad \text{uniformly for }s\in K.
11521: \]
11522: \end{theorem}
11523: 
11524: \begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
11525: This is a standard estimate in trace-ideal theory: the map $A\mapsto \det(I-A)$ is continuous in trace norm on bounded subsets of $\mathcal{T}_1$.
11526: One convenient inequality is
11527: \[
11528: \bigl|\det(I-A)-\det(I-B)\bigr|
11529: \le \|A-B\|_1\,\exp\!\bigl(1+\|A\|_1+\|B\|_1\bigr),
11530: \]
11531: valid for trace-class $A,B$.
11532: See, e.g., Simon's trace-ideal monograph \cite{SimonTraceIdeals}.
11533: \end{proof}
11534: 
11535: \subsection{Determinantal HP--GRH theorem}
11536: \label{sec:determinantal_HP_GRH_theorem}
11537: 
11538: We can now state the exact determinantal theorem used to close the Hilbert--Pólya $\Rightarrow$ GRH argument in this manuscript.
11539: 
11540: \begin{theorem}[Determinantal Hilbert--Pólya closure for GRH]
11541: \label{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH}
11542: Fix a completed $L$--function $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ holomorphic in $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11543: Assume that for each cutoff level $N$ one can construct:
11544: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
11545: \item a finite-dimensional reversible totally positive transfer matrix $T_{N,\varpi}(s)$ realized by a positive wiring diagram built from the toric degeneration of surface-order determinantal semi-invariants;
11546: \item a corresponding self-adjoint Hilbert--Pólya matrix $H_{N,\varpi}$ obtained from $T_{N,\varpi}$ by symmetrization and modular-Hamiltonian extraction (Corollary~\ref{cor:cycle_reversal_self_adjoint});
11547: \item an operator-valued holomorphic family $A_{N,\varpi}(s)$ (finite rank, trace class) whose Fredholm determinant agrees with the Hilbert--Pólya approximant:
11548: \[
11549: F_N(s;\varpi)=\exp(\alpha_{N,\varpi}+\beta_{N,\varpi}s)\,
11550: \det\!\Bigl(sI_{d_N}-\bigl(\tfrac12 I_{d_N}+ i H_{N,\varpi}\bigr)\Bigr)
11551: = \det\!\bigl(I-A_{N,\varpi}(s)\bigr);
11552: \]
11553: \item a limiting trace-class family $A_\varpi(s)$ such that $A_{N,\varpi}(s)\to A_\varpi(s)$ in trace norm uniformly on compacta in $0<\Re(s)<1$, and
11554: \[
11555: \Lambda(s,\varpi)=\det\!\bigl(I-A_\varpi(s)\bigr)
11556: \quad\text{in }0<\Re(s)<1
11557: \]
11558: (up to an exponential renormalization factor that does not create zeros).
11559: \end{enumerate}
11560: Then GRH holds for $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$.
11561: 
11562: Moreover, if the convergence in (d) is uniform in $\varpi$ on compact subsets of a parameter family, then the conclusion holds uniformly in that family (a GRH-strength statement).
11563: \end{theorem}
11564: 
11565: \begin{proof}
11566: By (a)--(b), each approximant $F_N(s;\varpi)$ is of Hilbert--Pólya form, hence all its zeros lie on $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:zeros_on_critical_line_finite}).
11567: By (c)--(d) and Theorem~\ref{thm:fredholm_det_continuity}, the functions $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ converge to $\Lambda(\,\cdot\,,\varpi)$ uniformly on compacta in $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11568: Therefore Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh} applies and forces all nontrivial zeros of $\Lambda$ to lie on the critical line.
11569: 
11570: Family-uniformity is exactly Proposition~\ref{prop:family_hurwitz_grh}.
11571: \end{proof}
11572: 
11573: 
11574: \begin{theorem}[Determinantal Hilbert--P\'olya $\Rightarrow$ (Artin holomorphy \emph{and} GRH) from a single convergence statement]
11575: \label{thm:hp_convergence_implies_holomorphy_and_grh}
11576: Let $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ be a completed $L$--function for which the Dirichlet series/Euler product converges absolutely in $\Re(s)>1$
11577: (hence $\Lambda$ is holomorphic there), and assume $\Lambda$ is known \emph{a priori} to admit meromorphic continuation to $\C$
11578: (e.g.\ by Artin formalism/Brauer induction in the Artin case).
11579: 
11580: Assume that one constructs a sequence of Hilbert--P\'olya determinantal approximants $F_N(s;\varpi)$ with the following properties:
11581: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
11582: \item (\textbf{HP form / zero location}) Each $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ has all zeros on the critical line $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$
11583: (e.g.\ $F_N(s;\varpi)=\det(sI-(\tfrac12 I+iH_{N,\varpi}))$ with $H_{N,\varpi}$ self-adjoint, as in Section~\ref{sec:determinantal_HP_GRH_theorem}).
11584: \item (\textbf{Holomorphy of approximants}) Each $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ is holomorphic on the strip $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11585: \item (\textbf{Uniform convergence}) $F_N(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)\to F(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ uniformly on compact subsets of $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11586: \item (\textbf{Matching on an overlap}) There exists a nonempty open set $U\subset\{\Re(s)>1\}$ such that
11587: \[
11588: F(s;\varpi)=\Lambda(s,\varpi)\qquad \text{for all }s\in U.
11589: \]
11590: \end{enumerate}
11591: Then:
11592: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
11593: \item $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ is holomorphic on $0<\Re(s)<1$ (in particular, Artin holomorphy holds in the critical strip for the given $\varpi$); and
11594: \item all nontrivial zeros of $\Lambda(s,\varpi)$ in $0<\Re(s)<1$ lie on $\Re(s)=\tfrac12$ (GRH for $\Lambda$).
11595: \end{enumerate}
11596: \end{theorem}
11597: 
11598: \begin{proof}
11599: By (ii)--(iii), $F(\,\cdot\,;\varpi)$ is holomorphic on $0<\Re(s)<1$ by the Weierstrass theorem (Proposition~\ref{prop:weierstrass_holomorphy_from_approximation}).
11600: By (iv), $F$ agrees with $\Lambda$ on a nonempty open subset of the domain where $\Lambda$ is holomorphic; by the identity theorem, $F$ is the analytic continuation of $\Lambda$ to $0<\Re(s)<1$.
11601: Since $F$ is holomorphic on the whole strip, $\Lambda$ has no poles there, proving (a).
11602: 
11603: For (b), combine (i) with (iii) and apply Hurwitz' theorem in the form stated as Theorem~\ref{thm:hurwitz_hp_implies_grh}.
11604: \end{proof}
11605: 
11606: \begin{remark}[What this theorem does (and does not) solve]
11607: Theorem~\ref{thm:hp_convergence_implies_holomorphy_and_grh} is \emph{unconditional as a logical implication}:
11608: it reduces holomorphy and GRH to the construction of a determinantal HP approximation that matches $\Lambda$ on an overlap.
11609: What is hard (and where all arithmetic content lives) is establishing the existence of such a sequence and proving (iii)--(iv).
11610: The purpose of the surface-order/dessin and invariant-theory machinery earlier in the manuscript is to make (iv) a \emph{geometric matching problem in determinantal coordinates} rather than an ad hoc analytic miracle.
11611: \end{remark}
11612: 
11613: 
11614: 
11615: 
11616: \begin{remark}[Where the determinantal input from Schreiber/CCKW enters]
11617: Theorem~\ref{thm:determinantal_HP_GRH} is intentionally ``modular'':
11618: it separates what is \emph{representation theory/invariant theory} (toric degeneration, determinantal semi-invariants, Cartan determinant cycle factorizations) from what is \emph{analysis} (trace-class limits and determinant continuity) and what is \emph{operator algebra} (total positivity $\Rightarrow$ self-adjoint modular generators).
11619: The Artin/surface-order package (Theorem~\ref{thm:artin_determinantal_toric_package}) is precisely the input ensuring that the arithmetic Euler factors can be encoded by determinantal invariants that survive base change and behave functorially in $\varpi$.
11620: \end{remark}
11621: 
11622: \begin{remark}[Why weak-$\ast$ convergence is the right minimal target]
11623: Even when trace-norm convergence is analytically hard, weak-$\ast$ convergence of the normalized states $\rho_{N,\varpi}$ is a \emph{physically meaningful} minimal target:
11624: it is exactly the convergence notion preserved by CPTP coarse-graining channels.
11625: Once weak-$\ast$ convergence is established, the remaining problem is to upgrade it to the trace-class control required by Theorem~\ref{thm:fredholm_det_continuity}.
11626: This upgrade is where renormalization, decay of cycle weights, and toric positivity are expected to do real work.
11627: \end{remark}
11628:
